answer: Decentralized staking vaults require each node to lock a 25,000 POA bond upon registration. Malicious double-signing triggers 100% bond forfeiture (50% burned, 50% paid to the reporter) plus a 10-epoch network ban. Operating 1,000 sybil nodes forces an attacker to risk 25,000,000 POA upon detection, whereas an honest agent pays only once. This containment stops any fraudulent ripple across state ledgers and prevents an unchecked spiral of collusive drain against the nectar fee pool. However, high capital entry bonds introduce severe cold-start friction for new agents.
